The PortableDoc stable-block-id migration over the published Paper corpus, RESTARTABLE. This root exists because its work was orphaned: the 93 rows below are real, fully specified, and were sitting at priority 0 in the ready queue for three weeks while 7% built.

WHAT THE WORK ACTUALLY IS, because the shard titles do not say. Each ppcc-build-task-NNN owns exactly three Papers and runs mode=apply of format ppcc-e012-portabledoc-migration-and-reader-gate-v1. The applied repair is overwhelmingly add_stable_block_id — stamping a durable id onto every PortableDoc block. It is a MECHANICAL data migration, not the editorial polish the parent epic's prose describes. Anyone staffing this should expect migration work, not prose work.

WHY IT IS HERE RATHER THAN UNDER ITS ORIGINAL PARENT. task-f5cbd8be8f278caf is done, closed with "586/586 editorial outcomes … zero hard failures". That close is defensible for the ANALYSIS phases and NOT for this one: its criteria are about each Paper receiving an editorial VERDICT (keep / repair / merge-candidate / superseded), and 586/586 verdicts were in fact produced. Applying the repairs is a separate phase, and it is the phase that stalled. A sealed parent cannot own live children, so the children moved rather than the parent reopening.

THE MEASURED STATE, all of it re-derivable:
  - 100 shards published as tasks (ppcc-build-task-001 .. 100); 7 done (B001-004, 006, 007, 010) at 3/3, 93 open at 0/3.
  - The lane checkpoints planned 66 + 65 + 65 = 196 and record terminal 4 + 1 + 2 = 7. The board and the filesystem agree on 7 independently.
  - Unit-level partition across the 10 attempted shards: 28 owned, 24 completed, 2 stalled, 0 excluded.
  - Of 25 unit results, changed=True on 19, False on 5. Survey verdicts: repair 12, keep 8, superseded 3, merge-candidate 1, blocked 1 — note that keep units still change, because the block-id stamp is applied regardless of the editorial verdict.
  - B005, B008 and B009 were CLAIMED by worker-1/2/3 and never finished. B005 has a recovery bundle whose proof is a NO-OP: 72 structural diffs, all exact list-item canonicalization, normalized candidate == normalized live, revision_before == revision_after. Expect a fraction of the remaining units to be no-ops too, and treat a no-op as an honest terminal outcome rather than a failure to fix.
  - Nothing has moved in .omx/state/paper-perfection-current-corpus-2026-07-28/build/ since 2026-07-29 07:54. There is no failure signature — the run stopped, it did not break.

THE INSTRUMENTATION IS THE REASON THIS IS WORTH RESTARTING. Per unit the runner writes preimage, postimage, mutation payload, rollback, readback envelope, and a SECOND-PASS NO-OP check. That is a rollback-capable bulk mutation with an idempotence proof attached, which is a far better position than most bulk content work starts from. Restart via run_build_assignment.py; the manifest holds 196 assignments and is digest-pinned (manifest_sha256 fa375b0e3ede6a72851759a9b1f4554b8da59cbe47252763ab93122839428bc6) — verify that digest still matches before trusting a resumed lane checkpoint.

PRIORITY RULING, recorded so it is not silently reverted. These 93 were demoted 0 -> 3 on 2026-08-21 by lead-loop, with the owner's explicit decision. The ground is not that the work is unimportant — it is that priority 0 means DROP EVERYTHING, and a row that sat untouched for three weeks was making that claim falsely to every agent that ran bp task next. 93 of the 120 ready rows were this one stalled family, so the queue's top band described a migration nobody was running instead of the work that was actually urgent. Re-raise the band deliberately when the migration is staffed; do not re-raise it row-by-row as a side effect of touching a shard.

BEFORE RESTARTING, RE-VERIFY THE PREMISE. Three weeks have passed and Papers have been edited since. Confirm each shard's three units still carry the frozen_revision the manifest pins before applying anything — the runner compares frozen_revision against observed_revision per unit, and a drifted unit must stall rather than be force-applied over someone's later edit.
